# Spendesk API Documentation

> Guides, recipes and API reference for the Spendesk API: spend data, accounting exports, invoices, cards, webhooks, and an MCP server for AI assistants.

## Documentation: Getting started
- [Introduction](https://developer.spendesk.com/reference/general.md): What the Spendesk API lets you do — spend data, reference data, accounting, purchasing, cards and webhooks — and where to start as a customer, a partner or on the demo.
- [Getting access](https://developer.spendesk.com/reference/getting-access.md): Which access you need, who sets it up in Spendesk, and which scopes to ask for.
- [Quickstart](https://developer.spendesk.com/reference/quickstart.md): Make your first Spendesk API call in five minutes — with Postman, curl or a short script.
- [How to Authenticate](https://developer.spendesk.com/reference/how-to-authenticate.md): Get an access token with an API key (customers) or OAuth2 (partners), how long it stays valid, and how to renew it.
- [Organisation-level access (multi-entity)](https://developer.spendesk.com/reference/organisation-level-access.md): Use one token for every entity of a Spendesk organisation: list its companies, then scope each call to the entity you want.
- [Postman collection](https://developer.spendesk.com/reference/postman.md): Guidance on using our public Postman collection.
- [Using this documentation with an AI assistant](https://developer.spendesk.com/reference/using-the-docs-with-an-ai-assistant.md): How an AI assistant or coding agent can read this documentation: llms.txt, the Markdown version of every page, the documentation's MCP server and the OpenAPI definition — and which source to trust.

## Documentation: Conventions
- [Scopes](https://developer.spendesk.com/reference/scopes.md): Every OAuth scope of the API and what it opens, how to request a token with fewer scopes, and how to get the experimental ones.
- [Pagination](https://developer.spendesk.com/reference/pagination.md): How list endpoints paginate — page-based, cursor or offset — the page-size limits, and what a page past the last one returns.
- [Error Handling](https://developer.spendesk.com/reference/error-handling.md): The error model (code, detail, source, correlation ID), the HTTP codes the API returns, and partial success (207) on bulk updates.
- [Rate Limiting](https://developer.spendesk.com/reference/rate-limiting.md): The API's rate limits, the response headers that report what is left, and how to design an integration that avoids 429 errors.
- [Data Types](https://developer.spendesk.com/reference/data-types.md): Formats used across the API: ISO 8601 dates and date-times in UTC, ISO 4217 currency codes, and amounts in minor units.
- [Versioning & Deprecation](https://developer.spendesk.com/reference/versioning-deprecation.md): How the API is versioned, which changes are backwards compatible, and how deprecations and sunsets are announced (Deprecation header).
- [Using webhooks (experimental)](https://developer.spendesk.com/reference/using-webhooks.md): Receive a call when a payable is created or prepared or a settlement is created (experimental): access, set-up, events and payload.

## Documentation: Use cases
- [Building an accounting integration](https://developer.spendesk.com/reference/building-an-accounting-integration.md): Connect Spendesk to an ERP or accounting system: keep its chart of accounts in Spendesk, post every prepared expense and payment into it, and tell Spendesk what was posted.
- [Exporting accounting data](https://developer.spendesk.com/reference/exporting-accounting-data.md): Get your purchase and bank journals out of Spendesk, and tell Spendesk what you exported so nothing is exported twice.
- [Managing purchase orders](https://developer.spendesk.com/reference/managing-purchase-orders.md): Follow committed spend, create purchase orders from your ERP or procurement tool, track their billing, and close or cancel them.
- [Following card spend](https://developer.spendesk.com/reference/following-card-spend.md): Follow your company's cards, the spend requests behind them, and the card payments — settled and declined.
- [Connect an AI assistant (MCP)](https://developer.spendesk.com/reference/connect-an-ai-assistant-mcp.md): Ask your AI assistant about your company's spend, invoices and accounting — and act on them — through the Spendesk MCP server.
- [Set up Claude, ChatGPT or Dust (MCP)](https://developer.spendesk.com/reference/mcp-set-up-claude-chatgpt-dust.md): The admin steps, on the Spendesk side and in the assistant, to make the Spendesk MCP server available to your team — and what each user does next.
- [Using the AI assistant safely (MCP)](https://developer.spendesk.com/reference/mcp-using-the-assistant-safely.md): What protects you when an AI assistant works with your Spendesk data, what to know about AI assistants before allowing them to act, and how to roll it out safely.
- [Assistant actions and safety (MCP)](https://developer.spendesk.com/reference/mcp-actions-and-safety.md): What an AI assistant connected to Spendesk can change, what cannot be undone, and what keeps it in check — to read before you tick a write permission.
- [MCP tool reference](https://developer.spendesk.com/reference/mcp-tool-reference.md): Every tool of the Spendesk MCP server: what it does, whether it reads or acts, the permission it needs, and whether its action can be undone.
- [MCP errors and limits](https://developer.spendesk.com/reference/mcp-errors-and-limits.md): What each error from the Spendesk MCP server means and what to do about it: missing permissions, roles, companies, stale versions, large queries and rate limits.
- [What is Spend Data?](https://developer.spendesk.com/reference/how-to-use-spend-data.md): Spendesk's accounting model: payables, settlements and bank fees, how they relate, and a payable's lifecycle from approval to export.
- [Retrieving Spend Data](https://developer.spendesk.com/reference/retrieving-snapshots-of-payables.md): Get payables in bulk with an asynchronous snapshot: request it, poll until it is complete, then read it while it stays cached.

## Documentation: Recipes
- [Running the recipes](https://developer.spendesk.com/reference/running-the-recipes.md): Short, ready-to-use answers to everyday finance questions — with Postman, an AI assistant, or a small script.
- [Export a month of spend to a spreadsheet](https://developer.spendesk.com/reference/export-a-month-of-spend-to-a-spreadsheet.md): Every expense of a month in a CSV: supplier or employee, amount, cost center, bookkeeping status and receipt.
- [List the invoices due this week](https://developer.spendesk.com/reference/list-the-invoices-due-this-week.md): The approved supplier invoices to pay in the next days, overdue ones first, with the total still due per currency.
- [Month-end close checklist](https://developer.spendesk.com/reference/month-end-close-checklist.md): What is still missing before closing a month: receipts, exports to accounting, approvals, failed exports.
- [Check the wallet balance](https://developer.spendesk.com/reference/check-the-wallet-balance.md): The wallet balance, what is available or committed, and the latest wallet loads.
